business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Dilutive Revenue-Based Financing for Digital Brands

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención de la blanqueo de capitales y la financiación del terrorismo (as amended by Ley 7/2021 and subsequent regulations); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se establece el Registro de Beneficiarios Finales del Registro Mercantil Central

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Habilitación)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and controllers against Spanish, EU, UN, OFAC, and domestic sanctions/PEP lists using certified databases; full identification and verification of beneficial ownership structure per AML/CFT guidelines

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Registry of Companies)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory Spanish language with exclusive use of Latin alphabet; no transliteration permitted for standard corporate names
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the Ministry of Justice within one month of rejection notice, followed by optional judicial review before the relevant commercial court

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible when the registered office is a verifiable physical address operated by a licensed service provider (e.g., professional office or specialized corporate service provider); purely virtual addresses without physical presence are generally rejected
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; unannounced inspections occur only in cases of suspected non-compliance or AML red flags, with documentation verification prioritized

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal consultation, incorporation drafting, and SL formation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff plus prevailing market benchmark for limited liability company setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification, verification, and AML due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for enhanced AML/CFT services
Hague Apostille fees plus legalization charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office setup, annual compliance, and tax registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual service fee plus statutory filings

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the revised text of the Capital Companies Law (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, LSC) - artt. 21, 22, 33, 62-63, 78-83; and Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) for digital incorporation procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central; provincial Registro Mercantil of the company's registered office (under Ministry of Justice).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública) which must be inscribed in the Registro Mercantil within two months of notarial execution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For SL, shares must be fully subscribed and fully paid-up at formation. Minimum capital may be €1 under the Crea y Crece scheme; statutory default remains €3,000. Cash contributions are deposited in a Spanish bank account and credited before the deed is signed. Non-cash contributions must be described in annexes to the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION - We, the undersigned directors of [COMPANY] Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, acting singly and on behalf of the shareholders' unanimous consent, approve (i) the subscription list and payment of the fully subscribed share capital set out in the public deed of incorporation; (ii) the adoption of the Company's statutory registered office and address for purposes of filings and legal notices; (iii) the appointment of [Name] as Managing Director and [Name] as Secretary, each with full representation powers; and (iv) the authorization of the Managing Director to execute all registrations, tax filings, and banking mandates necessary to render this resolution operable under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (RDL 1/2010).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Certificate of Non-Conflict
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central via online CIRCE portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the negative name certificate (certificado de denominación social) application with three proposed company names. The Central Registry verifies absence of identical or similarly prohibited names. The resulting certificate is valid for three months and must accompany the subsequent notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Three proposed company names for [COMPANY] Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
Standard application form for negative name certificate
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is denied for identical or prohibited name, resubmit with alternative names; appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month if an administrative rejection is unjustified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notaría) chosen by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the name certificate is obtained, appear before a Spanish notary to grant the public deed of incorporation. Include bylaws, capital allocation, subscriptions, appointments of directors, and statements of paid-up capital. Deposit paid-up capital in a Spanish bank account and annex the deposit certificate to the deed. The notary applies for the provisional tax ID (NIF) within 30 days.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate evidencing deposit of paid-up capital
Identification documents of all founding members (DNI/NIE/passport)
Proof of address of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the draft deed, amend the articles and re-execute before the same or another notary; if the provisional NIF application is deferred, file Form 030 with the Tax Agency later.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first notarial copy of the deed for registration within two months from the deed date. The registrar reviews the formal and substantive legality of the incorporation, including capital, bylaws, and director appointments. Obtain the certified registration entry; the company acquires legal personality upon registration.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the deed of incorporation
Express written acceptance of office by all appointed directors
Standard registration fee form (Modelo 791) or online payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar suspends or denies registration due to subsistable defects, file corrected deed or supplementary resolution within the statutory term; against unjustified denial, appeal to the Provincial Mercantile Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive Tax ID and Censal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Sede Electrónica / local tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 (declaración censal) with the AEAT and attach the registration certificate issued by the Commercial Registry to obtain the definitive NIF. Declare the start of business activity, select applicable taxes (IVA, IS, IRPF withholding), and register as an obligated entity for anti-money-laundering purposes if conducting financing operations.
required_dossiers: Form 036 signed by the legal representative
Copy of the public deed and provisional NIF
Proof of the registered office address (lease or ownership certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT queries the form due to discrepancies, correct and resubmit within 10 business days; obtain a certification of consistency with the Commercial Registry if the censal data is contested.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial authority applicable; the entity performs non-industrial financial activity and will not register manufacturing establishments. Ministry of Industry oversight applies only to goods-controlled activities, which are outside scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal licencia de apertura or declaración responsable for office use (if physical premises); no industrial operation permit is required for the non-bank financing fund business model.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico - Secretaría General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt under Ley 21/2013 Annex III; non-polluting office-only activity without physical transformation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC or stack emissions projected; compliance is limited to general waste segregation under Ley 7/2022 and energy-efficiency obligations for office equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate for commercial premises under RSCIEI Regulation; workplace risk assessment and health-and-safety clearance under Ley 31/1995 (Prevención de Riesgos Laborales); occupancy certificate under municipal building regulations for office use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal https://www.agenciatributaria.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL entities receive NIF automatically upon registration with the Registro Mercantil Central; non-resident owners must appoint a tax representative and submit Form 036 via AEAT portal to obtain statutory TIN and VAT ID
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections; hybrid mismatch rules apply under EU ATAD directive, with limited opt-in regimes available for small enterprises

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time invoicing through SII (Sistema de Información Inmediata); API integration required for immediate transmission of invoices and digital stamping by AEAT

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate on goods exported outside the EU upon proof of dispatch and non-EU entry; offshore services to non-EU clients qualify under specific documentation rules
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims result in fines up to 200% of undue VAT, surcharges, and potential criminal prosecution; full retrospective clawback of refunds with interest

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating as the Spanish national competent authority within the Eurosystem, and charged with foreign-exchange statistics, capital-movement monitoring, and payment-system oversight under Law 19/2003 (Movements of Capital and Economic Transactions with the Exterior) and Bank of Spain Circular 1/2019 on statistical declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account operations. Spain maintains no exchange-control, prior-authorisation, or repatriation restrictions under Article 63 TFEU; capital inflows and outflows with the EU and third countries are liberalised, subject only to EU/UN sanctions and to declaratory (post-closure) statistical reporting to the Bank of Spain. Profit remittances and disinvestment proceeds are freely transferable after satisfaction of Spanish corporate income tax and non-resident withholding obligations: the general IRNR withholding rate for dividends/royalties to non-residents is 19%, reducible under Spain's double-tax treaties (including US, UK, Mexico, and LatAm treaties). Practical hurdles are documentary only: beneficial-ownership evidence, registrations in the Spanish Foreign Investment Register, and observance of tax-limitation rules (interest-deduction cap under Ley 27/2014 Article 16 and transfer-pricing arm's-length rules under Article 18).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline on export proceeds or foreign-currency receivables. Residents may freely hold and settle foreign-currency accounts both in Spain and abroad. A purely statistical declaration applies under Bank of Spain Circular 1/2019 (Form TE-001) for individual cross-border transactions exceeding EUR 50,000; this is an informational threshold and never a convertibility constraint.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR/USD Current Account and Treasury Cash-Pooling (capital escrow not statutorily required but offered for fund warehousing)
Operational Account with dedicated FX Conversion and Hedging Lines
Operational Account with extensive LatAm correspondent network and merchant collection rails
Operational Account via innovation/fintech onboarding channel (BStartup)
Operational Account (conservative underwriting for non-bank lender profiles)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability as supplementary liquidity and FX rails, with legal limits: EU-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (Wise Europe, Revolut, Qonto, OpenPayd, and similar PSD2/E-Money passporting entities) may lawfully hold float and execute FX for the SL, but they cannot provide licensed credit or act as the sole fiduciary treasury for a revenue-based financing fund. The SL should maintain at least one tier-1 credit institution account for regulatory credibility; EMIs resident in offshore non-EU jurisdictions are rated Low because Law 10/2010 Article 3 strict identification rules and correspondent de-risking make them unsuitable for primary treasury concentration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Requirement is bank-dependent but effectively mandatory: Spanish tier-1 banks generally require at least one in-branch or notarial face-to-face identification of the SL's managers/UBOs under Law 10/2010, although remote video identification is legally permitted when accompanied by enhanced due diligence and certified documentation. Non-resident directors and UBOs in a financial-investment vehicle are routinely asked for a physical appearance at a Spanish branch or before a notary, and a board-level or management-level interview covering business model, source of funds, and projected cross-border flows is standard for ISIC 6499 / Medium-Risk-Enhanced files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: classification as a professional lender or unregulated credit activity (prestamista/persona dedicada a la concesión de préstamos) under Law 10/2010, causing enhanced due diligence or refusal by conservative banks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish legal opinion confirming the SL's own-funds royalty-purchase and revenue-based financing model falls outside the Crowdlending Law (Ley 5/2015) and the Credit Institutions Law; audited financial statements; AML/CFT internal procedures manual; funds-flow model showing non-deposit-taking status; ISIC 6499 registration certificate; clean sanctions/PEP screening summary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: non-resident UBOs or investors held through offshore SPVs or LatAm shell holding structures, preventing transparent look-through of ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership-chain chart identifying all UBOs with >25% control registered in the SL's sub-28 book; apostilled constitutional documents; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations supported by tier-1 foreign bank statements; certificate of no adverse regulatory history from the UBO jurisdiction; virtual data-room access granted to the bank's compliance team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: mismatch between the SL's declared business scope and observed transaction flows, specifically unexplained inbound royalty repayments from multiple LatAm digital brands inconsistent with the financing pipeline.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed royalty-financing agreements and purchase contracts referencing each disbursement; collection schedule reconciling every repayment wire to its underlying disbursement; borrower onboarding files; CRS/FATCA self-certifications; Bank of Spain TE-001 statistical declarations proving regularity and traceability of cross-border movements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: PEP or adverse-media hits on shareholders, managers, borrowers, or correspondent counterparties in LatAm markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial PEP-screening reports with risk scoring and rationale; where a PEP is identified, senior-management approval record and enhanced due-diligence file; source-of-wealth documentation; borrower-side AML/ABC contractual covenants; negative-news investigation memorandum prepared by counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders fund the SL's equity via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR) carrying ISO 20022 purpose code 'INVS' (investment) or 'OGDP', with the SWIFT remittance narrative expressly citing 'Aportación de capital a sociedad española — Registro de Inversiones Exteriores' and the Bank of Spain statistical foreign-investment code for equity capital. For USD, the wire settles through the receiving bank's nostro with the SL's IBAN in the beneficiary field; no prior central-bank authorisation is required, but the SL must post-file the transaction with the Ministry of Economy and the Bank of Spain (declaración posterior via Form TE-001) and present the notarised capital-increase deed and NIF certificate to the beneficiary bank. Verification includes the originating bank's KYC adequacy, the exact source account matching the registered shareholder, and value-date FX conversion at the bank's published rate where currency differs.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: High-value disbursements to LatAm digital brands settle via SWIFT MT103 direct wires; MT202/MT202COV interbank cover payments are used where local correspondent clearing requires cover instructions; Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) apply only when borrower jurisdictions demand bank-confirmed trade instruments. Recurring revenue-share collections use Core SEPA Direct Debit for EEA obligors and Direct-Debit/ACH equivalent rails via licensed local partners in Mexico and Mercosur. The SL's treasury architecture should maintain a EUR concentration account in Spain, a USD nostro concentration account at a tier-1 Spanish/New York branch, and segregated receivable collection accounts in jurisdictions of the borrower base to avoid currency-conversion friction and sanctions-wire breakage.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF FX Forwards (compra/venta a plazo) documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or the ACI Spain Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras (CMOF)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing LatAm currencies (BRL, MXN, COP, CLP) for royalty flows from restricted-deliverability markets, settled in EUR or USD
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) matching USD-denominated royalty receivables to EUR floating-rate liabilities
FX Swaps (swap de divisas) for temporary conversion of inbound USD into EUR working liquidity with simultaneous re-purchase commitment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Call and Holding of Annual General Meeting for Approval of Annual Accounts (Junta General Ordinaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting (corporate organ; no regulatory filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within the first six months after the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year company, by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve accounts within the legal period makes directors jointly and severally liable; continued non-approval can trigger due-cause dissolution of the SL

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales: Balance, P&L, Statement of Changes in Equity, Notes and, if applicable, Management Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the general meeting approving the accounts; for calendar-year accounts, by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine under the Spanish Companies Act of €1,200–€12,000 for late filing; non-filing for two consecutive fiscal years triggers 'cierre registral' (blocking of further registry filings) and prevents the company from obtaining registry certificates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Form 200) and final settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months and 25 days after the tax year-end; for a calendar year-end SL, by 25 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharges of 5%–20% depending on delay plus late-payment interest; penalties for inaccurate returns from 50% to 150% of the improper tax amount; potential director liability in insolvency scenarios

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Statement (Declaración de Titular Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry and Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual accounts deposit, within one month after the annual approval meeting; also updated whenever a qualifying shareholding transfer changes ultimate ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty up to €30,000 for failure to identify, present or update the real owner; the Mercantile Registry may reject subsequent filings until the declaration is corrected

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization and Maintenance of Mandatory Corporate and Accounting Books (Libros Registros y Libros de Contabilidad)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Books must be closed annually and legalized before annual accounts deposit; for calendar-year companies, practical deadline is 30 April after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalized books cannot be used as evidence in commercial disputes; the registry may reject the deposit of accounts and directors remain exposed to civil and administrative liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SL must undergo an independent audit if, for two consecutive years, it meets at least two of the following: balance sheet assets over €4.0 million; annual net turnover over €8.0 million; average workforce over 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for public-interest entities, listed companies, entities required by their by-laws, and at the request of shareholders holding at least 5% of the share capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (PGC, Plan General de Contabilidad) per Real Decreto 1514/2007 as amended; consolidated financial statements of groups follow EU-endorsed IFRS under Regulation (EC) 1606/2002; annual accounts must be expressed in euros.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year the SL must confirm to the Mercantile Registry the actual natural persons who directly or indirectly own more than 25% or exercise ultimate control; the annual UBO statement is made together with the deposit of annual accounts. Any transfer of SL quotas must be recorded in the notarized Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios) before the transfer is opposable to the company, and the UBO confirmation must be updated if the transfer alters ultimate ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors and of Appointment/Resignation Terms (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board Meetings (Libro de Actas)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $650 – $1,800 typical annual Spanish SL registered office, legal representation and compliance-casa fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500 – $8,500 typical fee for a small or mid-sized non-listed SL with non-bank royalty financing activity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate for ordinary companies. A newly incorporated company may generally apply a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory eligibility conditions and exclusions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax incentives may include the 15% newly incorporated company rate, research and development credits, technological innovation credits, deductions for investments in certain qualifying assets, capitalization deductions, and tax-neutral restructuring regimes. The reduced rate is unavailable where the company is part of an existing business group or is not genuinely newly incorporated under the applicable rules. Interest deductibility, loss utilization, and certain tax credits are subject to statutory limitations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Spanish Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where available, or an authorized tax representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is generally due within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the normal filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the deadline falls on a non-business day, the period extends under the applicable procedural rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, tax identification number (NIF), legal form, tax period, registered office, economic activity, group status, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent does not replace the Spanish SL's NIF or registered-office details. Report the Spanish SL as the taxpayer and disclose non-resident ownership only in the relevant ownership, related-party, or group schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before Spanish Corporate Income Tax as recorded in the statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish entity's approved statutory accounts. Do not substitute consolidated group profit, foreign parent profit, or cash-flow figures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions and deductions for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, impairment, depreciation, provisions, financial expenses, related-party adjustments, and other tax-specific differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes and payments to non-resident related parties must be classified under Spanish deductibility, withholding, beneficial-ownership, and transfer-pricing rules. Treaty relief does not automatically make an expense deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt dividends and capital gains, where statutory participation, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the participation percentage, holding period, foreign corporate tax burden, beneficial ownership, and anti-hybrid or anti-abuse conditions for non-Spanish subsidiaries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unused Spanish tax losses brought forward and utilized in the current period, subject to applicable taxable-base limitations and the minimum taxable-base rules for larger taxpayers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign group losses cannot be entered as Spanish tax losses. Maintain evidence of the original Spanish tax-loss returns and observe ownership-change and anti-avoidance restrictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments, loss utilization, and applicable rate selection, including any qualifying newly incorporated company rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Spanish SL rate, not the rate applicable to the non-resident shareholder. The 15% rate requires separate eligibility analysis and supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research and development, technological innovation, double-tax relief, employment-related, environmental, or other legally available credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require evidence of foreign tax paid or accrued, the relevant income, and the applicable limitation. Treaty entitlement and Spanish domestic credit rules must be reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance Corporate Income Tax payments, Spanish withholding suffered, and other payments credited against the final liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only amounts legally attributable to the Spanish SL and supported by AEAT certificates or payment records. Withholding suffered by a foreign shareholder is not a credit of the Spanish SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax payable, refund, payment method, and bank details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance, direct debit or electronic payment reference, refund account, and authorized filing details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A refund account may be outside Spain only where accepted by AEAT procedures. The filing must be authenticated by the Spanish taxpayer or an authorized representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, changes in equity, cash-flow information where applicable, tax reconciliation, related-party information, and other annexes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent consolidation packages do not replace Spanish statutory-account data. Keep reconciliations between Spanish accounts, management accounts, and group reporting.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax due may attract a fixed procedural penalty, generally reduced where voluntarily corrected before formal notice. Late payment normally triggers surcharges of 1% plus 1% for each completed month of delay during the first 12 months, followed by a 15% surcharge after 12 months, plus statutory late-payment interest. Deliberate or materially incorrect filing may result in penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on concealment, intent, and aggravating circumstances.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax payment on account, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment periods, normally April, October, and December
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ordinary filing periods are 1 to 20 April, 1 to 20 October, and 1 to 20 December. Large companies and taxpayers using the alternative taxable-base method may be subject to specific calculation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, and payment-period code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the Spanish SL as taxpayer. The non-resident investor is not the taxpayer for the SL's advance payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-period tax-liability method or current-period taxable-base method, where legally applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the method required by Spanish law based on turnover and group status. Do not use a foreign parent calculation unless it is only supporting information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Reference tax liability or current-period base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-period Corporate Income Tax liability or current-period taxable base and applicable percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign group entities and foreign taxes unless specifically included under a Spanish statutory mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for permitted payments and the resulting advance payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain the Spanish accounting and tax reconciliation supporting every claimed credit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing payment-on-account filings may generate late-payment surcharges, interest, collection costs, and procedural penalties. Underpayments may be assessed with tax penalties of approximately 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount where the conduct constitutes an infringement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, Informative return for related-party transactions and transactions with tax havens, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the normal deadline is 30 November of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, company name, tax period, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files for its own related-party transactions, including transactions with foreign shareholders, group companies, directors, and associated enterprises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nature of transaction, counterparty, country, amount, valuation method, and transaction type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify royalty, financing, management, guarantee, cash-pooling, and revenue-based financing transactions with foreign related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions exceeding statutory quantitative or category-based thresholds, including transactions under the same valuation method and with the same related party where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a transaction-by-transaction ledger even where Modelo 232 filing is not triggered. Do not split contracts or invoices to avoid reporting thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions with jurisdictions included in the applicable Spanish non-cooperative-jurisdiction list or otherwise subject to special disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain current jurisdiction classification before payment, and document commercial purpose, beneficial ownership, substance, and tax treatment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing, or materially incorrect information may attract fixed penalties per omitted or incorrect data item, subject to statutory minimums and maximums, in addition to transfer-pricing assessments and penalties where taxable income is understated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 216 and annual Modelo 296 for withholding and reporting on income paid to non-residents without a Spanish permanent establishment, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Modelo 216: monthly or quarterly depending on payer status; Modelo 296: annual information return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 216 is generally filed within the first 20 calendar days following the relevant month or quarter. Modelo 296 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of January for the preceding calendar year, subject to the applicable AEAT calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish SL NIF, name, fiscal period, and withholding-agent status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL is the withholding agent when it pays dividends, interest, royalties, or other Spanish-source income to a non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recipient name, tax identification number, residence country, income type, gross amount, exemption or treaty code, and withholding amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain and retain the recipient's tax-residence certificate, beneficial-owner evidence, and legal basis for any reduced rate or exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic rate, treaty rate, exemption, gross income, tax withheld, and payment date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty relief at source only where documentation and beneficial-ownership requirements are satisfied; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and permit the recipient to seek a refund where available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit tax may make the Spanish SL liable for the unpaid withholding, statutory interest, and penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the amount not withheld or remitted. Informative-return omissions may incur additional fixed penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish company to a non-resident, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU or EEA parent may be exempt under the Spanish implementation of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring at least a 5% participation, a minimum one-year holding period or commitment to hold, qualifying corporate status, subject-to-tax conditions, and anti-abuse compliance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify treaty eligibility, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse requirements where relevant, and retain corporate, ownership, and substance evidence. The Spanish payer files Modelo 216 and reports the payment in Modelo 296. Where relief was not applied at source, the non-resident may generally seek a refund through Modelo 210, supported by the residence certificate and payment documentation. Treaty access does not apply to conduit arrangements, artificial structures, or recipients lacking beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic non-resident taxation commonly applies a 24% rate to royalties and a 19% rate to interest, subject to statutory exceptions, recipient status, and treaty provisions. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty and interest rates, often to a range of 0% to 10%, but the applicable rate must be confirmed under the specific treaty. Qualifying intra-EU royalty and interest payments may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, generally requiring qualifying corporate status, minimum direct or group participation, a minimum holding period, subject-to-tax conditions, and anti-abuse compliance. Spanish withholding may also apply to service fees or other payments depending on source and permanent-establishment rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is generally required where related-party transactions with the same related person or entity and of the same type, valued under the same method, exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and category rules. A Master File is generally required for Spanish entities belonging to a group with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 45 million. Related-party transactions may also be reportable in Modelo 232 under separate thresholds, including material transaction-category thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a single standalone Economic Substance Regulation equivalent to certain offshore regimes. Substance is nevertheless required under general anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership principles, the principal-purpose test in treaties, EU anti-abuse law, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, and the Spanish anti-fraud framework. A royalty or financing company should maintain appropriate personnel, decision-making authority, premises or operational capacity, risk control, capitalization, documentation, bank-account control, and commercially credible functions. Pass-through arrangements, circular cash flows, back-to-back financing, excessive leverage, and royalty payments to entities lacking effective control create significant challenge risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax evasion and fraudulent return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing revenue, overstating deductions, fabricating expenses, using false invoices, or intentionally understating the Spanish taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, plus tax, interest, and collection costs. If the tax fraud exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax and period, criminal tax fraud may arise, with imprisonment generally from 1 to 5 years and a fine of one to six times the defrauded amount. Aggravated cases may carry imprisonment from 2 to 6 years and a fine of two to six times the amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability for unpaid tax where statutory management-liability conditions are met, criminal liability for intentional participation, disqualification from public office or management in applicable criminal proceedings, and liability for restitution and fines. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require judicial authorization or a specific legal basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, interest, guarantees, management fees, or revenue-based financing returns to shift Spanish profit to a foreign related party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make a primary transfer-pricing adjustment, impose tax, interest, and documentation or valuation penalties, and apply penalties commonly calculated by reference to the incorrect adjustment or omitted information. Repeated or deliberate manipulation may support tax-fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for negligent or intentional approval of abusive transactions, criminal exposure where the conduct constitutes tax fraud, and liability for destruction or falsification of supporting records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, or other Spanish-source income to a non-resident without withholding, without a valid residence certificate, or by applying an exemption without satisfying beneficial-ownership and anti-abuse conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish SL may be assessed for the unpaid withholding, late-payment interest, and penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the amount not withheld or remitted. Incorrect Modelo 216 or Modelo 296 filings may produce additional penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives may be pursued for avoidable non-compliance where statutory subsidiary liability requirements are met. Intentional concealment may create criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing funds through the Spanish SL without personnel, decision-making, risk control, or commercial purpose, followed by immediate onward payment to a foreign owner or affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty or EU exemptions may be denied, withholding may be reassessed, deductions may be disallowed, and general anti-abuse, transfer-pricing, and controlled-foreign-company rules may apply. Interest and penalties may be added.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil and, in serious intentional cases, criminal liability for knowingly implementing an artificial structure or distributing funds while concealing the true recipient.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed financial activity and unauthorized lending
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting regulated banking, payment, investment, collective-investment, consumer-credit, or deposit-taking activity without the required authorization, particularly where the business model moves beyond proprietary corporate financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanctions may include cessation orders, public enforcement measures, fines, and restrictions on activity. Conduct regulated as unauthorized banking, payment services, investment services, or collective investment may also trigger criminal consequences under applicable legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal administrative or criminal liability for knowingly operating regulated activities without authorization, as well as civil claims from customers, investors, and creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained funds, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring source-of-funds concerns, structuring payments, failing to retain records, or failing to report suspicious transactions where the entity is subject to Spanish AML obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious infringements may result in substantial fines, including fines up to EUR 10 million or up to 10% of the preceding year's total turnover for the obliged entity, together with public reprimands, authorization restrictions, management removal, or other statutory measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and directors may receive personal fines, be removed or disqualified where legally available, and face criminal liability for money laundering or terrorist financing. Criminal money laundering may carry imprisonment generally from 6 months to 6 years, together with fines and confiscation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False accounting, document destruction, or fabricated commercial records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining sham contracts, falsifying board approvals, backdating invoices, concealing beneficial owners, destroying accounting records, or creating false evidence for tax or transfer-pricing purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments, accounting sanctions, evidentiary presumptions, administrative penalties, and criminal offences relating to falsification of documents, accounting fraud, or obstruction may apply. Confiscation and restitution may be ordered in criminal proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, accountants, and authorized signatories may be prosecuted personally for intentional falsification, obstruction, fraud, or participation in the underlying tax offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit distribution and insolvency misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or repatriating capital while the company lacks distributable profits, is balance-sheet insolvent, cannot meet debts, or uses related-party payments to prejudice creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Improper distributions may be recoverable from shareholders and directors, with director liability for restoration of corporate assets and creditor losses. Insolvency proceedings may impose liability for the insolvency estate deficit and disqualification from managing companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to return distributions, compensate the company or creditors, bear insolvency deficits, and face disqualification. Fraudulent asset stripping may also generate criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using nominees, undisclosed trusts, circular ownership, or false shareholder records to conceal the ultimate beneficial owner or evade tax, sanctions, AML, or regulatory controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Benefits may be denied, transactions may be reassessed, assets may be frozen or confiscated, and administrative or criminal sanctions may apply under tax, AML, sanctions, and corporate law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and nominees may face personal civil, administrative, and criminal liability, including fines, restitution, disqualification, and imprisonment where concealment supports money laundering, fraud, or sanctions evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sanctions evasion and prohibited cross-border payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making payments to sanctioned persons or jurisdictions, disguising the beneficiary through intermediaries, or using royalty or financing contracts to circumvent European Union or Spanish restrictive measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transactions may be blocked, funds confiscated or frozen, licenses revoked, and administrative or criminal sanctions imposed under applicable Spanish and European Union sanctions legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal fines and criminal prosecution where they knowingly authorize, facilitate, or conceal sanctions breaches.
